gramont1529.summary: Gramont writes to Montmorency as Clement VII sets out for Bologna (October 1529): he vouches for the Pope's secret alignment with France; Clement dreads the general council and plans to grant it in principle and then stall it, offers to feign illness on the road to wait for the Admiral Chabot, fears soothsayers who foretell his deposition or death "du costé de" the Emperor, and had a dream before leaving Rome (enclosed). Orange is dealing to restore the Medici in Florence against Pisa and Livorno going to the Emperor.
gramont1529.en:
f. 45r. Monseigneur, I see that, both by my letters of the thirteenth and of the seventh of September [and by
the] despatch of the bull of the four tenths and other things which the King of Navarre's maître d'hôtel brings you,
you will have been made sure that, if I have heretofore written to the [King] and to you of the good will of Our Holy
Father, I have done it more with clear knowledge of it by deeds than by light belief or any other extraordinary
wish that moved me to it. And I can tell you that, the further I go, the more I confirm my opinion, inasmuch as I
see ordinarily and clearly that the greatest wish our said Holy Father has is to remain in true friendship and union
with the [King];

system: Homophonic substitution on graphic signs ('Gramont's cipher (1529)', Lasry's table; siblings fr. 3040 f. 16 and Clair. 330 f. 53), several homophones for common letters, doubled-letter and COM/CON signs, a few nulls and code signs for persons.
